Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 97 (DataBank): operator own dedicated page confirmed the existing address and added IT capacity and sqft, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Granite Point Campus SLC4, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 14860 S Pony Express Rd, Bluffdale, UT 84065, and states 3.67 MW of critical IT load and 20,740 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank SLC4 in Bluffdale, Utah, publishes 3.67 MW of IT capacity, operated by DataBank.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 367 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 92 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DataBank SLC4. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Utah has 9 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 8 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 51.69 MW. DataBank SLC4 contributes 3.67 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
